title: When AI hallucinates facts about individuals: Personal data and accuracy under the GDPR
headline: AI hallucinations and personal data accuracy under the GDPR
summary: Generative AI systems can produce entirely false and fabricated statements about real individuals, creating significant legal risks. This issue came to light in March 2025 when NOYB filed a complaint with Norway's data protection authority against OpenAI over a fabricated criminal record generated by ChatGPT. Legal experts are now examining whether such outputs violate the data accuracy principle under Article 5(1)(d) of the EU General Data Protection Regulation.
why_it_matters: Organisations deploying generative AI must address the risk that probabilistic models can fabricate damaging personal information, triggering potential liabilities under data protection accuracy principles.

quotes.text: Indeed, in March 2025, NOYB filed a complaint with Norway's data protection authority, Datatilsynet, against OpenAI after ChatGPT generated an output that claimed a Norwegian man had murdered two of his children and had been sentenced to prison.

The growing number of legal disputes involving AI hallucinations shows that hallucinated outputs can have real-world consequences while simultaneously exposing providers and deployers of generative AI systems to significant legal risk.

classification.significance_reason: Provides a useful analysis of legal risks and GDPR compliance regarding AI hallucinations, though it is commentary rather than binding regulatory guidance.
